# deed_relationship_type (Resource)

A custom Deed relationship type (built-in types such as `runs_on`, `depends_on` or `owned_by` are owned by Deed and cannot be managed). Requires an installation `admin` (or owner) token. Endpoint kind constraints can only be narrowed while no live relationship would violate them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "deed_relationship_type" "powers" {
  name         = "example.com/powers"
  inverse_name = "powered_by"
  title        = "Powers"
  description  = "Electrical power supply."
  from_kinds   = ["example.com/ups"]
  to_kinds     = ["server", "storage", "network"]
  impact       = "reverse" # what it powers depends on the UPS: losing the UPS affects them

  attributes_schema = jsonencode({
    type = "object"
    properties = {
      outlet = { type = "integer", minimum = 1 }
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Type name: a lowercase identifier, optionally prefixed by a domain (`example.com/backs_up`). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `title` (String) Display name, e.g. `Backs up`.

### Optional

- `attributes_schema` (String) Optional JSON Schema (2020-12) for relationship attributes, as a JSON string (use `jsonencode`). Compared semantically.
- `cardinality` (String) `many` (default) or `one` target per source entity.
- `color` (String) Edge color as `#rrggbb`.
- `default_evidence` (String) Evidence class of relationships reported by importers: `structural` (default) or `observed`.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `directed` (Boolean) Whether the relationship has a direction (default `true`).
- `from_kinds` (Set of String) Kinds allowed as the source endpoint (empty = any).
- `impact` (String) Impact propagation in the map: `forward` (default), `reverse`, `both` or `none`.
- `inverse_name` (String) Name of the inverse direction shown on the target, e.g. `backed_up_by`.
- `to_kinds` (Set of String) Kinds allowed as the target endpoint (empty = any).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The relationship type name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import deed_relationship_type.powers example.com/powers # type name
```
